options.text: Renders the component matched by the current URL

questions.explanation: <RouterView> is the outlet where Vue Router renders whichever component matches the current route.

questions.prompt: How do you read a dynamic route parameter :id inside a component?
questions.explanation: useRoute() returns the current route; its params object holds dynamic segments, e.g. route.params.id.

questions.prompt: Why should you use <RouterLink> instead of a plain <a href> for internal navigation?

options.text: It navigates client-side without a full-page reload
Plain <a> tags don't work in Vue

questions.explanation: RouterLink handles the click to navigate within the SPA without reloading the page; a plain <a href> triggers a full reload.

questions.prompt: With createWebHistory (clean URLs), the server must serve index.html for unknown paths — a so-called SPA ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: History mode needs a SPA fallback so deep-link refreshes serve index.html instead of 404ing. Hash mode avoids this.

questions.prompt: What is a navigation guard like router.beforeEach used for?

options.text: Running logic (e.g. auth checks) before a navigation completes, to allow, cancel, or redirect it

questions.explanation: Guards run before a route change; returning false cancels it and returning a location redirects — commonly used to protect authenticated routes.

questions.prompt: Order these steps to set up Vue Router.
questions.explanation: Define routes, create the router with a history mode, register it on the app with app.use, then render matched components with <RouterView>.
